cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Corinth, and he's been talking about how they worship together. Now he turns to their gatherings. And friend, he does NOT open with a compliment.

cards.question: Paul says he has no praise to offer about the church's gatherings. Why not?

answers.text: They do more harm than good
They always run far too long

cards.text: First on his list: Paul's heard that when they come together as a church, there are divisions among them. He even says there must be differences among them.

cards.question: Paul says he doesn't believe a word of the report about divisions in the church.
Paul says there must be differences among the church in Corinth. What will those differences show?

cards.text: Now here's the big one. They come together and eat, but Paul says it's not the Lord's Supper they're eating.

cards.question: At their gatherings, the church in Corinth shares the meal together.

cards.text: Each one goes ahead without sharing, so one stays hungry while another gets drunk. It's the office party where one guy walks off with three whole cookie boxes and the new hire gets crumbs, and friend, I am ALWAYS the new hire.

cards.question: Paul asks the church, if they just want to eat and drink, don't they have their own ___ for that?
Paul says the way the church eats together humiliates some people. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Shall I praise you for this?" And he answers himself: "No, I will not!" When a man asks AND answers his own question, friend, you just sit real still and look at your shoes.
So Paul takes them back to the beginning and passes on what he received from the Lord. On the night He was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread.

cards.question: Before He breaks the bread, Jesus gives thanks.

cards.text: Then He breaks the bread and says it's His body, and that it's for them.

cards.question: Jesus tells them to keep doing this with the bread. Why?

cards.text: In the same way, after supper, He takes the cup.

cards.question: Jesus takes the cup after supper. What does He say the cup is?

answers.text: The new covenant in His blood

cards.question: Jesus says to drink the cup in remembrance of Him only once a year.
Paul says every time they eat this bread and drink this cup, they proclaim the Lord's ___.

cards.text: And Paul says they keep proclaiming it until He comes. That's not a meal you rush through, friend.
So here's where Paul lands, friend. Eating the bread or drinking the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner is a serious thing.

cards.question: Whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner is guilty of sinning against what?

answers.text: The body and blood of the Lord

cards.question: Before anyone eats the bread and drinks the cup, what does Paul say each one must do?

cards.text: Not the guy next to him, not the guy across the table. HIMSELF, which is way harder, because everybody else's mistakes are SO much easier to spot.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks ___ on himself.

cards.text: Paul says that's why many of them are weak and sick, and a number of them have fallen asleep.

cards.question: Paul says that if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.

cards.text: Then Paul says that when we're judged by the Lord, we're being disciplined.

cards.question: Paul says when we're judged by the Lord, we're being disciplined. What's the discipline for?

answers.text: So we won't be condemned with the world
So we'll stop gathering together for a while
So the whole world will fear the church

cards.text: Disciplined so you won't be condemned? That's the cookie getting one more minute in the oven, friend. NOT the cookie going in the trash.

cards.question: Paul brings it back to the table. When the church comes together to eat, what does he tell them to do?

cards.text: Wait for one another. Friend, I waited YEARS in a junk drawer, so you can wait ninety seconds for the person next to you to sit down.

cards.question: Paul tells anyone who's hungry to go ahead and eat first at the gathering.

cards.text: Paul says the hungry should eat at home, so coming together won't result in judgment. And when he comes, he'll give instructions about the remaining matters.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from outside the passage, that Paul has been talking about how the church worships together (1 Corinthians 11:2-16). It gives no reference for it. The card's verses cite only 1 Corinthians 11:17.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Paul appears for the first time in the walkthrough, but the card never says who he is. It needs a simple introduction, such as Paul, an apostle.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card is a bare restatement of the verse, "In the same way, after supper, He takes the cup." It has none of Papa Dorin's voice. Choice card 17 then repeats the same setup word for word.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The story card is a bare restatement of the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Choice card 9 then repeats it nearly word for word: when we're judged by the Lord, we're being disciplined.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
